title: Draft: Improving ssh decryption and dissection
description:
Add decryption.
Add retrieval of cookie/private key in DSB.
Add dissection of STFP protocol.

This code is based on #16054

Working algorithms: (mostly ssh-audit v2.3.1 recommendations)
1. key exchange algorithms (kex) [essential for decryption]
- [x] diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256
- [x] diffie-hellman-group16-sha512
- [x] diffie-hellman-group18-sha512
- [x] diffie-hellman-group14-sha256
- [x] diffie-hellman-group14-sha1
- [x] diffie-hellman-group1-sha1
- [x] curve25519-sha256 / curve25519-sha256@libssh.org
2. host-key algorithms (key) [not necessary for decryption]
- [ ] rsa-sha2-256 / rsa-sha2-512
- [ ] ssh-ed25519
3. encryption algorithms (ciphers) [essential for decryption]
- [x] chacha20-poly1305
- [x] aes128-ctr / aes192-ctr / aes256-ctr
- [x] aes128-cbc / aes192-cbc / aes256-cbc
- [x] aes128-gcm / aes256-gcm
4. message authentication code (mac) [not necessary for decryption]
- [ ] umac-128-etm
- [ ] hmac-sha2-256-etm / hmac-sha2-512-etm

Test file: [ssh-test.zip](/uploads/f739af39b3cf2ca49210104fe5ae9f81/ssh-test.zip)
- ssh.pcapng / ssh.txt a short ssh session, and its key file
- sshS.pcapng the same short ssh session, but the key is embedded in the capture file
- sftp.pcapng / sftp.txt a short sftp session, and its key file
- sftpS.pcapng the same short sftp session, but the key is embedded in the capture file

The SFTP protocol is sufficiently independent from the SSH protocol, I think it is worth moving it to a new SFTP dissector. To call that dissector, it would probably suffice hard-coding the subsystem check and call into the SFTP dissector (`sftp_handle = find_dissector("sftp");` in the proto handoff routine). Hopefully this separation improves maintainability.

Relevant specs on which I based the above suggestion:
- https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-ietf-secsh-filexfer-13
- https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4254#section-6.5

To create a test sample without leaking private info (MAC addresses, IP addresses, usernames, SSH public keys), I suggest creating a Docker container or VM. In there you can run sshd with a custom config and generate a new ssh keypair for testing. To limit captured data to the SSH session, use a capture filter such as `tcp port 22` for example.
